_comment: ROLE -> MODEL POLICY. Portable intent; versioned; no machine-local state.
Every role ships as "track-latest" -- a deliberate, legal choice meaning
'accept Claude Code's Default for this role, and accept that the tier may
move when the account roster changes'.  THE CEO ASSIGNS REAL TIERS ON MERGE
REVIEW.  This branch delivers the mechanism; the tier assignments are the
CEO's decision and are intentionally left unmade.
Legal values for roles.<role>.model:
"track-latest"                 accept Default; tier may move (recorded as a choice)
a tier alias                   opus | sonnet | fable | haiku -- tier pinned, version tracks
an exact model id              e.g. claude-opus-5[1m] -- fully pinned
NOTHING model-related may go in canonical/settings.json -- that file is a
live symlink the app writes back to, so a model key there becomes a phantom
diff.  scripts/doctor.sh check 10a FAILs on it.  Per-machine pins belong in
~/.claude/settings.local.json (untracked).
roles.<role>.permission_mode is OPTIONAL and is normally ABSENT. When it is
absent the wrapper passes no permission flag and settings.json
permissions.defaultMode governs -- that is the intended steady state, and
the reason the wrappers stopped hardcoding --dangerously-skip-permissions.
Set it only to make a role deliberately differ from the settings default.
Legal values are whatever the installed claude accepts for --permission-mode
(2.1.236: acceptEdits | auto | bypassPermissions | manual | dontAsk | plan);
the wrapper reads that list from `claude --help` and refuses an unknown value
before creating anything.  CC_PERM_MODE=<value> overrides one launch.
known_models is the change-detection baseline: doctor check 10c WARNs on any
model in the account roster (~/.claude.json additionalModelOptionsCache) that
is not listed here.  Adding a model to this list IS the act of deciding that
track-latest still applies to it.
